## Key Takeaways

1. The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index® increased by 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, far above the forecast of 81.2.
2. The Present Situation Index increased by 8.6 points to 120.4.
3. The Expectations Index increased 6.9 points to 72.6, staying below the recessionary 80.0 threshold since February 2025.

Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index [...] The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index measures the consumers attitudes and confidence in the economy, business conditions, and labor market, with higher readings indicating higher optimism. The general assumption is that when consumers are more optimistic they will spend more and stimulate economic growth

The Conference Board said Tuesday that its consumer confidence index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October from 84.2 last month. September’s reading was the lowest in the board’s survey since April 2014 and below the lowest level reached during the pandemic.

Yet Americans remain flustered by the economy after five years of elevated inflation, potentially posing a risk to President Donald Trump and Republicans in the midterm elections next Tuesday. results.content:
Consumer sentiment ticked slightly lower in October, hovering near record-low levels, according to the end-of-month reading from the University of Michigan’s survey.

The survey’s headline index came in at 48, versus 46.3 in the preliminary October reading and down from 48.1 in September. It is the final reading from the survey before November’s midterm elections, with voter frustration about the economy at the center of many campaigns.
